Let $x$ be a Boolean list and let $n$ be a natural number. If the encoded edge relation
is symmetric on vertices below $n$, the construction assigns a regular multigraph on the
vertex set $\	ext{Fin}(n)$ of degree $2^{\operatorname{size}(n)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length-loop entry from multiplication]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_len}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_len}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_1, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_10, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_13, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_14, Complexity.LogProg.adEx, Complexity.LogProg.adP, Complexity.LogProg.adY, Complexity.LogProg.mulA, Complexity.LogProg.mulB, Complexity.LogProg.mulEx, Complexity.LogProg.mulR, Complexity.LogProg.ups_ad, Complexity.LogProg.ups_mul}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and $\sigma$ a
register state whose fifteen values are at most $B$. Suppose its scratch-sum,
scratch-product, and walk-length values are all zero, and $100n^4+10n\le B$, where $n$
is its vertex-count value. Assume that for every $a,b\le B$, the program started at $w0$
on input $x$, with the row and inner counters set to $a,b$, the scratch-sum set to
$10n$, the scratch-product set to $n(10n)$, and the walk length set to $n(10n)(n(10n))$
(all other values unchanged), has all live register values at most $B$, terminates along
every sequence of choices, and has acceptance probability $q$ and rejection probability
$1-q$ for every choice length at which every sequence of choices halts. Then the program
started at $lc(0)$ from $\sigma$ has those same bounded-register termination and
probability properties.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Averaging over a block of random choices]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_coin}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_coin}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.choose, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.half, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jz_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_6, Complexity.LogProg.adEx, Complexity.LogProg.adP, Complexity.LogProg.adY, Complexity.LogProg.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.cpEx, Complexity.LogProg.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.size_eq_succ, Complexity.LogProg.upA, Complexity.LogProg.ups_ad, Complexity.LogProg.ups_cp}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input, $B$ a natural-number register bound, and $F$ a function from
natural numbers to rational numbers. For every natural number $\tau$ and register state
$\sigma$, suppose the scratch register equals $\tau$, every register of $\sigma$ is at
most $B$, and $2(\sigma_{nx}+1)2^{\operatorname{size}(\tau)}\le B$. Suppose also that
for every natural number $i$ with $\sigma_{nx}2^{\operatorname{size}(\tau)}\le
i<(\sigma_{nx}+1)2^{\operatorname{size}(\tau)}$, and every pair of natural numbers
$b,e\le B$, the program has probabilistic semantics $F(i)$ from the designated loop
state with registers $nx=i$, $tmp=0$, $b=b$, and $e=e$. Then the program from the
designated initial state with register state $\sigma$ has probabilistic semantics
$$\frac{\sum_{j<2^{\operatorname{size}(\tau)}}F(\sigma_{nx}2^{\operatorname{size}(\tau)}+j)}{2^{\operatorname{size}(\tau)}}.$$
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Less-than loop from its two cases]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_lt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and $\sigma$ a
register state whose fifteen values are at most $B$. If the random-index value of
$\sigma$ is less than its vertex-count value, assume that for every $a\le B$ the program
started at the index routine for the walk site, with the row counter set to $a$ and all
other values as in $\sigma$, has all live register values at most $B$, terminates along
every sequence of choices, and has acceptance probability $q$ and rejection probability
$1-q$ for every choice length at which every sequence of choices halts. If the
vertex-count value is at most the random-index value, assume the same property for every
$a\le B$ when started at the continuation label with the row counter set to $a$. Then
the program started at the less-than loop label from $\sigma$ has those bounded-register
termination and probability properties.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Average over padded edge slots]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.sum_slots}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.sum_slots}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph, Randomized.padDegree}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $G$ be an undirected multigraph with vertices indexed
by $	ext{Fin}(n)$ and degree $2^{	ext{size}(n)}$, and let $f$ assign a rational number
to each vertex. For any vertex $v$, the sum of $f$ over the neighbors in the slots
indexed from $0$ to $2^{	ext{size}(n)}-1$, with out-of-range slots contributing $0$,
divided by $2^{	ext{size}(n)}$, equals the sum of $f$ over all edge slots at $v$ divided
by the degree.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Walk reachability probability]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ups_walk}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ups_walk}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PSem.acc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.call_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.PSem.rej, Complexity.LogProg.UPS, Complexity.LogProg.UPS.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.UReg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.Le, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.reg, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_0, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_4, Complexity.LogProg.UReg.v_8, Complexity.LogProg.cpDst, Complexity.LogProg.cpEx, Complexity.LogProg.cpSrc, Complexity.LogProg.ixCol, Complexity.LogProg.ixEx, Complexity.LogProg.ixRow, Complexity.LogProg.pathOr_bit, Complexity.LogProg.sum_slots, Complexity.LogProg.ups_coin, Complexity.LogProg.ups_cp, Complexity.LogProg.ups_index, Complexity.LogProg.ups_lt, Complexity.SymRest, Complexity.inEdge, Complexity.pathEdge, Complexity.rowMajor_lt, Complexity.upGraph, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb_succ, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb_zero, Randomized.padDegree, Randomized.padDegree_le, Randomized.padNbr}
\difficulty{6}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $n$ be a natural number, and suppose the encoded
adjacency relation is symmetric on vertices below $n$. Let $t\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and
suppose $2|x|+2\le B$ and $2n+2+2n^2\le |x|$. For every natural number $k$, register
state $\sigma$, and vertex $v\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ such that $\sigma.L-\sigma.st=k$, every
field of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.n=n$, $\sigma.cur=v$, $\sigma.t=t$, and
$\sigma.st\le\sigma.L$, the program started at state $w0$ with register state $\sigma$
has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability equal to the probability that a
uniformly chosen length-$k$ walk on the padded regular multigraph reaches $t$ from $v$.
\end{theorem}
